column2: Om Tat Sat is held to be the threefold designation of Brahman; sacrifice, charity and similar acts give men enjoyment and liberation.
The fruit of action is threefold: undesired, desired and mixed; it comes after death to those who do not renounce, but never to renouncers.
The tamasic arises from attachment to action, from delusion, trouble and fear; the rajasic and sattvic from desire and from freedom from desire. These are the five causes of action.
The seat, the doer, the instruments of many kinds, the threefold separate efforts, and fate as the fifth, are here.
Knowledge that sees one is sattvic; knowledge that sees separateness is rajasic; knowledge of no real aim is tamasic; action without desire is sattvic.
Action for desire is rajasic; action from delusion is tamasic. The doer who is equal in success and failure is sattvic; the rajasic is passionate.
The deceitful and lazy is tamasic; the intellect aware of what is to be done is sattvic; that which is for the sake of gain is rajasic; the opposite is tamasic.
Steadiness of mind is sattvic; that which desires delight is rajasic; the tamasic is in grief and the like; the face (happiness) of sattva goes to its end.
Happiness that is sweet at first is rajasic; that which is painful at the end is tamasic. From him is the activity of beings, by whom all this is pervaded.
Worshipping Vishnu by one's own duty, one attains perfection — by deed, mind and speech, in all conditions, always.
He who knows Vishnu as the world from Brahma down to a blade of grass, a devotee of the Lord, a Bhagavata, attains perfection surely.
Knowledge, discernment, faith, good fortune, excellent beauty — all that the mind desires is obtained by austerity.
There is nothing to meditate on equal to Vishnu, no austerity higher than fasting, no blessing like health, no river like the Ganges.
There is no kinsman save Vishnu, the teacher of the world. Hari is below, above and before, in body, senses and mind.
Remembering thus, whoever gives up his life becomes Hari. That Brahman from which all comes, in which all is established,
ungraspable, indescribable, firmly established, supreme — as the higher and lower forms, Vishnu dwells in every heart.
Some wish for the Lord of sacrifice, the Person of sacrifice, as supreme; some say Vishnu, some Hara, some Brahma, some Ishvara.
Some by the names of Indra and the rest, some say the sun, the moon, time. They say the world from Brahma to a blade of grass is Vishnu.
That Vishnu is the Supreme Brahman, from which one does not return. One attains it through great gifts of gold and the like, holy baths at sacred fords,
meditations, vows, worship and listening to dharma. Know the Self as the rider, the body as the chariot.
Know the intellect as the charioteer, the mind as the reins; the senses are called the horses, objects their paths.
The wise call the Self joined with senses and mind the enjoyer. He who lacks discernment, whose mind is always undisciplined,
does not reach the goal and goes to samsara; but he who has discernment, whose mind is always disciplined,
reaches that state from which he is not born again. The man whose charioteer is discernment and who holds the reins of the mind
reaches the end of the road, that supreme abode of Vishnu. Higher than the senses are the objects, higher than objects the mind,
higher than the mind the intellect, higher than the intellect the great Self, higher than the great the unmanifest, higher than the unmanifest the Person.
Than the Person there is nothing higher: that is the goal, the highest course. In all these beings the hidden Self does not shine forth,
but is seen by the subtle-sighted with a sharp, subtle intellect. The wise should restrain speech and mind in knowledge, and knowledge in the Self.
He should restrain knowledge in the great Self, and be tranquil in the Self. Knowing the union of Brahman and Self by yama and the rest, he becomes Brahman.
Non-violence, truth, non-stealing, celibacy, non-possession are the yamas; the five niyamas are purity, contentment, austerity,
study and worship of the Lord; posture such as the lotus; pranayama, mastery of breath; pratyahara, self-restraint.
Holding the mind on one auspicious object is called "dharana" by the wise, O Brahmin, because of its steadiness.
Repeated holding of the mind on those same objects is called "dhyana"; "samadhi" is the state of abiding as "I am Brahman, the Self".
As the space in a pot, when the pot is destroyed, becomes undivided from the sky, so the freed soul becomes Brahman, the real Brahman.
The soul thinks itself Brahman by knowledge and not otherwise; freed from ignorance and its effects, it is ageless and deathless.
Agni said: O Vasishtha, the verses sung by Yama give enjoyment and liberation to those who recite them. The final dissolution has been told, made of Vedanta and knowledge of Brahman.
By hearing it a Brahmin becomes learned in the Veda, a Kshatriya becomes lord of the earth, a Vaishya gains prosperity, and a Shudra gains health.
He who recites or hears daily, equal-minded and with mind on Vishnu, the Agneya Purana of Brahma — all calamities there perish.
Divine, atmospheric and earthly disturbances, evil dreams and spells, and whatever other evil there is — Keshava destroys it all.
For the man who recites or hears it, or worships the great book, the Agneya, the glorious Purana — he who hears it in the cold season...
...having worshipped it with fragrance and flowers, gains the fruit of the Agnishtoma; in winter, of the Pundarika; in spring, the Ashvamedha.
In summer the Vajapeya; in the rains the Rajasuya; in autumn the fruit of a thousand cows — such is the fruit of reciting it in each season.
He who reads the Agneya Purana with devotion before Hari, O Vasishtha, worships Keshava here with the sacrifice of knowledge.
Victory belongs to him in whose house is a book of the Agneya Purana, written and worshipped; enjoyment and liberation are in his hand.

Thus it was sung to me formerly by Hari in the form of the fire of time. The Agneya Purana is the seat of the twofold knowledge of Brahman. O Vasishtha, you will tell this twofold knowledge to devotees.
Vasishtha said: O Vyasa, the Agneya Purana, whose nature is twofold knowledge, was told to me by Agni, as it was told by Brahma and Vishnu.
Together with the gods and sages, Agni told me this Purana, showing all aims; the Agneya, O Gautama, is equal to Brahman.
He who reads, hears, meditates on, writes or has it written, or causes it to be heard or recited, or worships or keeps it...
...is freed from all sins, attains his wishes, and goes to heaven. He who has the Purana written and gives it to Brahmins...
reaches the world of Brahma and lifts up a hundred families. He who reads a single verse is freed from the mud of sin.
Therefore, O Vyasa, it should always be recited to disciples; the Purana that shows everything, with sages such as Shuka who desire to hear it.
The Agneya, read and contemplated, is auspicious and gives enjoyment and liberation. Homage to Agni, by whom the Purana was sung.
Vyasa said: O Suta, what Vasishtha formerly sang I have told you — the supreme state, the nature of higher and lower knowledge.
The Agneya form is hard to obtain; it is gained by the fortunate. Those who meditate on Brahman and the Agneya Purana have come to Hari.
Seekers of learning have gone to learning; seekers of kingship to kingship; the sonless have sons; the shelterless have gone to shelter.
Seekers of fortune to fortune; seekers of liberation to liberation; those who write it or have it written, sinless, have gone to prosperity.
O Suta, with Shuka, Paila and others, contemplate the form of the Agneya Purana; you will certainly attain enjoyment and liberation.
And recite the Purana to disciples and devotees. Suta said: By Vyasa's grace I have heard the Agneya Purana with reverence.
The Agneya is of the nature of Brahman. You sages, Shaunaka and others, in Naimisharanya, worshipping Hari the Lord,
standing with faith — therefore it has been told to you. The Agneya Purana, spoken by Agni, is equal to the Veda,
endowed with twofold knowledge of Brahman, great, giving enjoyment and liberation. There is no essence higher than this, no friend higher than this,
no book higher than this, no goal higher than this; no scripture higher than this, no revelation higher than this;
no knowledge higher than this, no tradition higher than this; no authoritative text is higher than this, nor any science.
No conclusion is higher than this, no greater blessing; no Vedanta higher than this; this Purana is supreme.
Nothing rarer is found on earth. In this Agneya Purana all sciences are shown.
All the avatars beginning with the Fish are sung here, with the Ramayana, the Harivamsha and the Mahabharata; nine creations are shown.
The Vaishnava scripture is sung, with worship, initiation and installation, the rite of the sacred thread, the marks of images,
the marks of temples, and mantras that give enjoyment and liberation; the Shaiva, Shakta and Saura scriptures with their aims;
diagrams, architecture, and various counsels; secondary creation is sung, the sphere of the cosmic egg;
the treasury of the worlds, continents, regions and rivers; the greatness of sacred places such as Gaya, Ganga and Prayaga is told;
the circle of the stars, astrology, the ocean of victory in war are sung; the Manvantaras and the duties of the castes;
impurity, purification of things, expiation are shown; duties of kings and of giving, and many vows;
legal procedure, rites of pacification, the rules of the Rigveda and others; the solar and lunar dynasties, archery and medicine;
music, the science of wealth, Mimamsa, the extent of Nyaya; the count and greatness of the Puranas, metre and grammar are remembered;
rhetoric, lexicon, phonetics and ritual are said to be taught here; the occasional, natural and final dissolutions;
Vedanta, the knowledge of Brahman, and eight-limbed yoga are told; hymns and the greatness of the Puranas — eighteen sciences are recalled.
The Rigveda and the rest are lower; the supreme knowledge is the imperishable. Brahman's form, with and without the world-spread, is declared.
This Purana, fifteen thousand verses in extent from a vast hundred crores, is always recited in the world of the gods by the gods.
Out of desire for the welfare of the worlds, Agni sang it in brief. Know, O sages Shaunaka and others, that all is Brahman.
Whoever hears it, or causes it to be heard, reads or has it read, writes or has it written, studies or recites it...
...a king should reverently honour the reciter of the Purana with gifts of cows, land, gold, clothes, ornaments and offerings.
By honouring him he gains the fruit of hearing the Purana. At the end of the Purana one should certainly feed Brahmins.
Stainless, with all aims attained, he goes to heaven with his family. Whoever gives a pen-holder for the book, thread, a bundle of leaves,
and a binding-band, cloth and the like, goes to heaven; whoever gives it becomes one of Brahma's world.

For one in whose house the book stands, there is no fear of calamity; he attains enjoyment and liberation. Remember the Agneya Purana, whose form is the Lord's. Suta, honoured by Shaunaka and the others, went to Hari.
